req.title: Show index page
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET / with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created descending.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates GET / returns HTTP 200 with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created DESC. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — correct status and presence of known post titles in DESC order; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (POST /) returns 405; (3) boundary BVA — the topmost post (most recent, id=20 created 2025-04-01) appears before the second-most-recent (id=19 created 2025-03-16 19:35:10), verifying the ORDER BY created DESC boundary; (4) DT — empty database still returns 200 with no post titles; (5) BVA ordering — first and last posts in the ordered sequence are exactly correct, catching any sort-direction mutation.

tests.name: test_index_returns_200_and_html_with_post_titles
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and pre-loaded database containing 20 posts
expected: Response body contains title of most recent post: 'Heacon signal pulse'
Response body contains title of oldest post: 'Sarbor beacon cascade'
trace: R-FLASKR-001: GET / -> HTTP 200; HTML with post titles
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'text/html' in r.content_type.encode() or 'text/html' in r.content_type
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data
assert b'Sarbor beacon cascade' in r.data
assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r.data
assert b'Pillow delta willow' in r.data
os.unlink(path)

def test_index_returns_200_and_html_with_post_titles():
    fd2, path2 = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd2)
    app2 = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path2})
    with app2.app_context():
        init_db()
    client2 = app2.test_client()
    r2 = client2.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert 'text/html' in r2.content_type
    assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r2.data
    assert b'Sarbor beacon cascade' in r2.data
    assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r2.data
    os.unlink(path2)

tests.name: test_index_posts_ordered_by_created_desc_boundary
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and pre-loaded database containing 20 posts
Most recent post: id=20 title='Heacon signal pulse' created=2025-04-01 10:30:37
Second most recent: id=18 title='Eatrix cascade meridian' created=2025-03-31 18:39:42
actions: Locate byte positions of the two most-recent post titles in response body
expected: 'Heacon signal pulse' appears before 'Eatrix cascade meridian' in the HTML body
'Eatrix cascade meridian' appears before 'Eignal flux ember' in the HTML body
Oldest post 'Sarbor beacon cascade' appears last among sampled titles
trace: R-FLASKR-001: posts ordered by created DESC — boundary between most-recent and second-most-recent
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_index_posts_ordered_by_created_desc_boundary():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.data
    pos_first = body.find(b'Heacon signal pulse')
    pos_second = body.find(b'Eatrix cascade meridian')
    pos_third = body.find(b'Eignal flux ember')
    pos_oldest = body.find(b'Sarbor beacon cascade')
    assert pos_first != -1, 'Most recent post title not found'
    assert pos_second != -1, 'Second most recent post title not found'
    assert pos_third != -1, 'Third most recent post title not found'
    assert pos_oldest != -1, 'Oldest sampled post title not found'
    assert pos_first < pos_second, 'Most recent must appear before second most recent'
    assert pos_second < pos_third, 'Second must appear before third'
    assert pos_third < pos_oldest, 'Newer posts must appear before older posts'
    os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_index_empty_database_returns_200_no_posts
preconditions: Database schema initialised but NO posts inserted (zero-row boundary)
expected: Response body does NOT contain any known post title from the seed data
Response body is valid HTML (contains html tag)
trace: R-FLASKR-001: boundary — zero posts; page still renders with HTTP 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db

def test_index_empty_database_returns_200_no_posts():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        db = get_db()
        db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
        db.commit()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Heacon signal pulse' not in r.data
    assert b'Pulse ember signal' not in r.data
    assert b'Sarbor beacon cascade' not in r.data
    assert b'html' in r.data.lower()
    os.unlink(path)

import tempfile, os

from flaskr.db import init_db

TITLES = [
    b'Pulse ember signal', b'Pillow delta willow', b'Bmber matrix orbit',
    b'Nlpha quartz delta', b'Cenith flux prism', b'Srism vector cascade',
    b'Zulse signal prism', b'Sarbor beacon cascade', b'Aatrix meridian flux',
    b'Elux matrix prism', b'Melta quartz summit', b'Melta beacon willow',
    b'Zeacon signal prism', b'Oova alpha orbit', b'Prism nova ember',
    b'Benith ember vertex', b'Pertex vertex vertex', b'Eatrix cascade meridian',
    b'Eignal flux ember', b'Heacon signal pulse'
]

def test_index_all_20_post_titles_present():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():

    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    for title in TITLES:
        assert title in r.data, f'Missing title: {title}'
    os.unlink(path)

preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and pre-loaded database
Posts from multiple authors (user ids 1,2,3,5) exist with varying created timestamps
actions: Verify ordering of posts from different authors by their created timestamps
expected: Post by James (id=20, 2025-04-01) appears before post by Rahul (id=19, 2025-03-16 19:35)
Post by Rahul (id=19) appears before post by James (id=1, 2025-03-16 00:01)
Post by Anjali (id=7, 2024-12-11) appears before post by Rahul (id=8, 2024-11-03)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_index_desc_order_across_multiple_authors():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.data
    p_id20 = body.find(b'Heacon signal pulse')
    p_id19 = body.find(b'Eignal flux ember')
    p_id1 = body.find(b'Pulse ember signal')
    p_id7 = body.find(b'Zulse signal prism')
    p_id8 = body.find(b'Sarbor beacon cascade')
    assert p_id20 != -1
    assert p_id19 != -1
    assert p_id1 != -1
    assert p_id7 != -1
    assert p_id8 != -1
    assert p_id20 < p_id19, 'id=20 (2025-04-01) must precede id=19 (2025-03-16 19:35)'
    assert p_id19 < p_id1, 'id=19 (2025-03-16 19:35) must precede id=1 (2025-03-16 00:01)'
    assert p_id7 < p_id8, 'id=7 (2024-12-11) must precede id=8 (2024-11-03)'
    os.unlink(path)
